messages:
ops-oncall: heads up — spike in 10:42 UTC: multiple services in us-west-2a started failing external calls, connection_reset / 502s. suspect NAT ephemeral port exhaustion. seeing degraded throughput to S3 and public model hosts.

deploy-bot: [ALERT] egress-error-rate: 1200/min; affected-tags=[model-pull, metrics-export]

maria_g: confirming. netstat/ss shows huge TIME_WAIT and sockets in SYN_RECV on natgw path. example from a noisy host: 
```
# ss -s
TCP: total 256000 (kernel 256000)
TCP: inuse 12345 orphan 0 tw 89000 alloc 3452 mem 12345
```

tarek: ok — two quick mitigations: 1) move model pulls to S3 via VPC endpoint (avoid NAT), 2) spin temporary NAT instances with larger ephemeral ranges while we scale managed NAT gw.

jordan_r: +1 on S3 endpoint. Also we should enable connection pooling for model pulls (keepalive / proxy) so each worker isn't doing 1000 short-lived TCPs. Can we flip a deploy of the edge fetcher to use our http-proxy sidecar?

maria_g: running command to check per-az NAT gw metrics and port usage:
```
aws ec2 describe-nat-gateway-telemetry --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=us-west-2a
```
returned: PortUsagePercent=98% on nat-0123456789abcdef0

ops-oncall: drafted immediate play: create 2x t3.medium NAT instances in us-west-2a, update route table to point to instance while AWS NAT scales. also put rate-limiting on non-critical model pulls.

pam: I'll open a quick infra ticket for dedicated egress proxy (HAProxy) with connection pooling + internal caching. If we keep relying on NAT gw for large fanout pulls, we'll keep hitting limits.

tarek: tactical CLI to create NAT instance (example):
```
# create instance
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0example --count 2 --instance-type t3.medium --subnet-id subnet-abc --associate-public-ip-address
# enable ip_forward and SNAT
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
```

jordan_r: note: NAT instances give us more ephemeral ports (per-instance), but also watch for asymmetric routing/health checks. We'll add a load-balancer in front of the instances for stability.

maria_g: quick short-term: added S3 VPC endpoint on the route table and patched model-pull config to prefer s3:// artifacts for 30% of traffic. measurable drop in NAT usage already.

ops-oncall: followups: (1) infra to create infra ticket for permanent egress proxy + LB, (2) product to gate model-pull concurrency and add caching, (3) SRE to consider reserved NAT capacity or multi-nat per AZ shaping. I'll update incident channel with status in 15m. :thumbsup:
